# Testing in a sandbox

This page is for developers who are about to publish a site package, or send it by pull request. A site package
writes a database and a whole set of settings when it is installed; the only safe place to try it is an installation
that exists for that purpose. This page shows how to make one, what to test, and how to remove it again.

7x and the Exponential Foundation strongly encourage you to submit your tested site package by pull request to
se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth: see [Contribute your site package](../contribute-your-site-package.md).
Reviewers will ask how you tested it.

## Make the sandbox

Use a separate checkout of Exponential 6.0, never the directory of a site that matters:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/se7enxweb/exponential.git sandbox-acme
cd sandbox-acme
composer install
```

The ways to get the code, and what `composer install` does, are in
[3. Getting the code](../../../install/03-getting-the-code.md).

Point it at the server that holds your test packages
([Pointing a site at your package server](pointing-a-site-at-your-package-server.md)):

```ini
# settings/override/package.ini.append.php
[RepositorySettings]
RemotePackagesIndexURL=https://packages.example.com/exponential/6.0/6.0.15
```

SQLite is the default database of `exp:install` and needs no server: the database is one file in
`var/storage/sqlite3/`, which makes the sandbox easy to throw away.

> **Warning**
> `exp:install --db-action=remove` (the default) empties the database first, and `--force` replaces an existing
> installation's database and settings. In a sandbox that is what you want; anywhere else it is not.

## Round 1: the archives

On your build machine, before anything is published:

```bash
tar -tzf acme_site.ezpkg | head                  # package.xml at the top
php ezpm.php validate /path/to/acme_site.ezpkg   # in the sandbox: the kernel's checks, nothing imported
```

See [Rebuilding with build.sh](rebuilding-with-build-sh.md#check-the-archive) and
[Validating a package before publishing](../requirements/validating-a-package-before-publishing.md).

## Round 2: a dry run

```bash
php bin/php/console exp:install --package=acme_site --print
php bin/php/console exp:install --package=acme_site --dry-run
```

`--print` shows the configuration and stops. `--dry-run` connects to the database and fetches your site package and
its requirements into `var/storage/packages/dryrun/`, which is removed again; it writes no database and no settings
([7.6](../../../install/07-console-install.md#76-dry-run-and-print)). It proves that your index can be read, every
archive downloads and imports, and every `<require>` is found. With a `kickstart.ini`:
`php bin/php/console exp:kickstarter run --dry-run` does the same ([6.7](../../../install/06-kickstarter.md#67-dry-runs)).

## Round 3: a full install

```bash
php bin/php/console exp:install --package=acme_site --url=http://localhost:8080 --random-password
```

Run it as the user the web server's PHP runs as, so the files it creates stay writable
([7.3](../../../install/07-console-install.md#73-options)). Then read the logs:

| Log | What to look for |
|---|---|
| `var/log/setup.log` | every step, download retries, warnings of your installer script |
| `var/log/kickstart.log` | the kickstarter's run (with `exp:kickstarter run`) |
| the summary printed at the end | site address, administration login, siteaccesses |

A post-install step that aborts the chain is reported: `eZSiteInstaller::abortedStep()` keeps its number and function
([Changing the installer script](changing-the-installer-script.md#post-install-steps)).

## Round 4: look at the result

- [ ] The front page and a few content pages render, in every siteaccess and language the package creates.
- [ ] The administration opens; **Setup > Packages** lists your packages as installed or imported, with no warnings.
- [ ] The content classes are those you expect (the class list of the administration), with their names in every language.
- [ ] The roles and policies your installer creates exist, and a test user of each role can do what it should.
- [ ] Pages that use layouts show their blocks.
- [ ] Install a second time with the `_clean` variant, if you ship one.
- [ ] Repeat the full install from scratch once more: an installer that only works the first time fails for the next
      person.

## Clean up

A sandbox left behind takes disk space and may run a server:

1. Stop any server you started for it (`exp:velocity stop`, or the `php -S` process).
2. Remove the sandbox directory once you have kept what you need (logs, screenshots).
3. Remove the test database if you used a database server instead of SQLite.

Keep a short note of what you tested and on which release: it belongs in the pull request description
([Contribute your site package](../contribute-your-site-package.md#test-the-install-in-a-sandbox-first)).
